To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a reporter system based on the LiaRS cell envelope stress-sensor of B. subtilisin is suitable for screening purposes to identify new cell wall biosynthesis inhibitors.
we developed a microtiter-plate based bioassay for monitoring lipid-II interfering stress and applied the system to identify new cell wall biosynthesis inhibitors.

the reporter strain developed by Mascher, Zimmer, Smith and Helmann (2004) is a valuable tool to monitor the action of antibiotics interfering with peptidoglyceran biosynthesis and to discover novel inhibitors thereof.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application for screening purposes of a microtitter-plate based bioassay for monitoring the interference of antibiotics and related compounds with the lipid II - cycle.
the development of new bioassays for the detection of cell wall active antibiotics and the identification of novel cell wall active compounds.
the identification of novel cell wall biosynthesis inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reporter system described here is suitable for the detection of cell wall biosynthesizing stress in general and for the identification of cell wall biosynthetically active antibiotics in particular.
our system can also be used for screening and identification of novel antibiotics interfering with cell wall biosynthesis.
the lipid II cycle is the primary cellular target for the lantibiotic class of antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our system can serve for screening purposes, e.g. to identify novel inhibitors of cell-wall biosynthesis.
the lipid II cycle is a target for a broad spectrum of lantibiotic and non-lantibiotic compounds.

the developed system is suitable to monitor cell wall stress in a microtiter format, thus providing a valuable tool to screen for novel cell wall biosynthesis inhibitors and to study the molecular mechanisms underlying cell wall stress responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
our reporter strain is a useful tool for the identification of cell wall biosynthesizing stress-inducing compounds.
the reporter system can be applied for the identification of novel cell wall biosynthesis inhibitors.
our system can detect a broad spectrum of cell wall biosyntheses stressors, which can also act by mechanisms other than inhibition of the lipid II cycle.
